dedupe_keys.name: wind toolkit continental u s wind resource and power series

description: The WIND Toolkit is a model-generated U.S. wind-resource and power-production collection published through the Open Energy Data Initiative and an AWS open-data registry. The managing laboratory describes gridded Weather Research and Forecasting outputs, turbine power estimates and aligned forecast series for more than 126,000 continental U.S. sites on a 2 km grid. Its main grid-modernisation page says 2007–2013, while its high-performance-computing page says the WRF model ran from 2007 through 2014; this review leaves the endpoint-year difference unresolved. The latter page says hourly instantaneous variables are broadly available, with five-minute wind speed and direction, so five-minute coverage should not be assumed for every field. The AWS registry states CC BY 3.0 U.S. and public access. No cloud object or time-series payload was opened. Simulation use includes wind-generation scenarios, transmission planning and weather-conditioned reliability studies. It complements data-era5-reanalysis with wind-power estimates for named generation sites. A caveat is that numerical weather and turbine power are model outputs, not measured production, and newer WTK-LED products are distinct releases.
